content.text:
I found and fixed it: all the bold text on the site (headings, buttons, prices, nav links, stat numbers) was rendering at roughly normal weight.

**Cause:** In `site/css/tokens.css`, the web font was declared with `font-weight: 400` only. The font file is Figtree, which contains every weight from light to black in one file. Because the declaration said 400, the browser used only the regular weight and faked bold for everything else, so the headings looked thin.

I checked this in the browser: the same text measured exactly the same width at weights 400, 600 and 800 (211.6px each), so no real bold was being drawn.

**Fix:** one line in `site/css/tokens.css:6`, changing `font-weight: 400;` to `font-weight: 300 900;`, which matches the font's full weight range.

**Checked:**
- The same text now gets wider as the weight goes up (211.6 → 215.5 → 221.3px), so real bold is being drawn.
- I took screenshots of all six pages at desktop (1280px) and mobile (390px) widths before and after. Bold text is bold again, and nothing else moved; the layouts looked fine before the change too.
- All 16 functional tests pass.

There's no git history from before the initial commit, so I couldn't see exactly what changed. This font problem was the only visual difference I found across the pages. If you meant something else, tell me which page and I'll look. The change isn't committed.

I found and fixed it: all the bold text on the site (headings, buttons, prices, nav links, stat numbers) was rendering at roughly normal weight.

**Cause:** In `site/css/tokens.css`, the web font was declared with `font-weight: 400` only. The font file is Figtree, which contains every weight from light to black in one file. Because the declaration said 400, the browser used only the regular weight and faked bold for everything else, so the headings looked thin.

I checked this in the browser: the same text measured exactly the same width at weights 400, 600 and 800 (211.6px each), so no real bold was being drawn.

**Fix:** one line in `site/css/tokens.css:6`, changing `font-weight: 400;` to `font-weight: 300 900;`, which matches the font's full weight range.

**Checked:**
- The same text now gets wider as the weight goes up (211.6 → 215.5 → 221.3px), so real bold is being drawn.
- I took screenshots of all six pages at desktop (1280px) and mobile (390px) widths before and after. Bold text is bold again, and nothing else moved; the layouts looked fine before the change too.
- All 16 functional tests pass.

There's no git history from before the initial commit, so I couldn't see exactly what changed. This font problem was the only visual difference I found across the pages. If you meant something else, tell me which page and I'll look. The change isn't committed.
